# Validation and external context {#sec-validation}

## Internal validation

### Calibration

All 21 anchor years hit every calibration target and meet every publication gate, with no constraint off by more than 0.000001%.
Effective sample sizes among taxation-of-benefits contributors never fall below
132 for OASDI and 86 for HI, against a floor of 50. In the six far-horizon
anchor years (2075-2100), they run 132-156 for OASDI and 107-127 for
HI. In 2100, they reach 153 for OASDI and 127 for HI, and the ten largest
household weights hold 3.4% of the total weight. We project federal income tax at about 8 to 10
percent of GDP across the horizon, in line with historical experience.

### Reform scoring

The metadata file of each of the 323 exact rows records that its run made the
manifest check, and each reform H5 hash matches the results file. In every anchor year, full
repeal reduces federal income tax by the full baseline revenue from taxing
benefits, and taxing all benefits raises revenue in every year. The exact 2062
anchors for the Roth swap and the phased Roth swap, which we score separately,
agree to the dollar in both the static and the labor-supply results.

## External benchmarks

We compare selected reforms with outside estimates from the Congressional Budget
Office, the Social Security Trustees, the Tax Foundation, and the Joint
Committee on Taxation [@cbo2024options; @ssa2024trustees;
@taxfoundation2024trump; @jct2024expenditures; @jct2025bonus]. These
organizations use different budget windows, scoring conventions, and baselines,
so we use the comparisons to check scale rather than point estimates.
